messages:
maria gonzalez: Quick kickoff — SignalBridge POC next Tue. They want a clear migration playbook from their current vendor to us. Main asks: prompt parity (edge cases), response drift mitigation, rate-limit/throughput parity, token/billing mapping, and answers to their security questionnaire (SOC2/KMS/VPC).

aj patel: I can own the prompt parity gauntlet. Will assemble ~60 representative prompts and expected acceptance criteria. @sophie ng can you wire the eval harness? :white_check_mark:

sophie ng: Yep. Plan: anonymize prompt set, run generation across competitor model and our target models, diff by exact-match + semantic similarity. Focus areas: stop sequences, streaming chunking, and repetition penalties.

chetan rao: I'll start drafting the security Qs. Ask SB to share the vendor questionnaire PDF so I can map answers. Need confirmation on: KMS provider, VPC peering options, audit log retention, and data residency controls.

maria gonzalez: They explicitly called out deterministic behavior for billing-sensitive flows. Recommend canary rollouts + golden prompt monitoring and automatic rollback thresholds. Also propose fallback policy: same-route fallback to smaller quantized model when capacity spikes.

aj patel: Note on billing/tokenization: their token counting and ours differ for some tokenizers. I'll include a short mapping example and an estimator script. Example snippet:```bash
# competitor -> redwood mapping (rough)
# competitor reported: 1200 tokens in prompt
# our tokenizer estimate: ~1120 tokens
python -c "from transformers import GPT2TokenizerFast as T; t=T.from_pretrained('gpt2'); print(len(t.encode('This is a test...')) )"
```

sophie ng: For response-drift detection, I'll add: daily regression checks on gold prompts, hallucination score threshold, and semantic drift alert if embedding cosine drops >0.06 vs baseline. Hook into console alerts.

chetan rao: For their security form: we'll confirm SOC2 in progress (if true), provide KMS integration docs, and propose a minimal IP allowlist CIDR template. Also outline our incident response SLA.

maria gonzalez: Pricing question came up: they want flat-rate mapping of request units. Suggest we show 1) per-request token estimate conversion table 2) discount tiers for reserved dedicated capacity. @aj can you generate a worked example for their 10M monthly prompt tokens?

aj patel: On it. Will include three scenarios: hosted pay-as-you-go, reserved dedicated slot with commit, and hybrid (hosted + dedicated fallback). Will show cost delta and expected latencies.

dawson (deploy-bot): canary env for sb-poc deployed to eu-west-1. 2 instances, model redwood/gptx-small, health ok.

maria gonzalez: Awesome. Final action items: - [ ] aj: prompt set + token mapping example - [ ] sophie: eval harness + regression alerts - [ ] chetan: security questionnaire draft - [ ] ops: prepare canary runbook + fallback policy doc. I'll compile a one-pager to send to SB by EOD Friday.

aj patel: Quick question — do we want to include a small compatibility shim for legacy stop_token behavior? Could save them prompt engineering time.

sophie ng: Yes, add a request/response normalization layer in the gauntlet. Simple mapping rules: normalize newline tokens, map legacy stop_token semantics -> our stop sequences. I'll document examples.

maria gonzalez: Perfect. If SB pushes back on any behavior differences, we'll show reproducible diffs and offer a 2-week prompt tuning window as part of the POC.

chetan rao: I'll ping legal about an NDA tweak for sharing production prompt samples.

maria gonzalez: Thanks team. I'll DM SB and schedule intro playbook review. :rocket:
